source.title: Data splitting improves statistical performance in overparametrized regimes
source.authors: Nicole Mücke; Enrico Reiss; Jonas Rungenhagen; Markus Klein

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test-risk behavior around a local interpolation threshold for distributed ridgeless linear regression, a different setting and sweep from the deep-network model-size claim.
record.gate_note: The reported sweeps vary the number of data splits, changing the local sample size and local overparameterization; they do not vary total training-set size, model size in deep networks, or training epochs. The paper also reports relative prediction-efficiency curves, which are not rows for the versions because that measure is not the test-error curve named there.
record.test_reason: The study's main aim is distributed learning, not double descent. Still, its real-data experiments (MSDYear, Fig. 2 right and Fig. 3) report a test-error peak at the local interpolation threshold d = n/M, then a decline as local overparameterization grows. That is a double-descent-shaped curve for minimum-norm linear regression, a new setting bearing on V4. The sweep axis is the number of splits M, which jointly changes the local samples-to-dimension ratio and the number of averaged estimators.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors' main conclusion is that in (locally) overparameterized ridgeless regression, the number of data splits acts as a regularizer trading bias for variance. They find an optimal number of splits improves both accuracy and computation, with bounds they call optimal and efficiency gains quadratic (finite-d) or linear (infinite-d) in the optimal split number. The double-descent peak at d = n/M is a secondary illustration (Fig. 2 right, Fig. 3, Theorem B.6).
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes and illustrates averaged minimum-norm ridgeless regression across data splits, rather than the original deep-network model-size, epoch, or total-sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error behavior changes with the number of splits and whether local estimators are underparameterized or overparameterized.

fits_no_version.finding: In globally overparameterized settings (simulated strong-weak features, Fig. 1 right; MSDYear with n = 45, Fig. 2 left), test error falls with more splits up to an optimal M. The number of splits acts as a regularizer trading bias against variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Averaging local minimum-norm interpolants over data splits regularizes overparameterized ridgeless regression, giving a risk minimum at an interior number of splits.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), 2021
record.problems: The plotted test-error values and uncertainty are not provided in the text. The reported interpolation behavior is for a distributed linear-regression setting and a split-count sweep, not the principal axes in V1–V3.
record.rows_left_out: Relative prediction-efficiency plots and comparisons in Section 6 and Appendix C were omitted because they report efficiency ratios rather than the test-error curve named by the versions. No other reported test-error result bearing on V4 was omitted.

untested.parts: No sweep over model capacity or parameter count. Only linear minimum-norm regression is tested, with no other model classes. Capacity is varied only indirectly through local sample size n/M under averaging.
Total sample size is fixed; only per-split samples change, confounded with averaging.
Effective ranks are used in bounds only; no test of peak-location prediction across axes.
The lower-bound peak height scales with noise variance τ̃², but noise is not varied experimentally. No test of regularization removing the peak.

missing.what: Test error versus number of machines for different spectral gaps (simulated, n = 200, d = 600). This is a test-error curve, not an efficiency ratio, yet it is not recorded.
MSDYear global-overparameterization experiment (n = 45, 100 repetitions): splitting reduces test error.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3. This is a new setting (distributed linear regression) rather than a different method aimed at the same question. Evidence for V4 is figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty. The 'capacity' axis is the local ratio d/(n/M), and the second descent coincides with averaging more estimators, so the curve is not a clean capacity sweep. Peer-review venue in the record (AISTATS 2021) is not stated in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Total training sample size is not increased; the reported change is in samples per local estimator as the data are split.
The reported curve is for distributed ridgeless linear regression as the number of splits changes, not a capacity sweep across model classes.
Effective ranks and effective dimension are used in bounds, but a single effective-complexity measure is not tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample axes.
No controlled test of label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective parameter count to assess whether the curve becomes an ordinary U shape.

rows.subject: distributed ridgeless regression estimator β̄M
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of data splits M and reported test error as local overparameterization changed.

conditions.value: total sample size larger than the number of parameters

rows.note: The text says test error increases while local estimators are underparameterized and starts decreasing after local overparameterization appears at M = n/d = 15. Curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Subject is correct: averaged minimum-norm linear estimators on MSDYear, d = 90. The swept axis is the number of splits M, not model capacity, so local overparameterization is confounded with averaging over M estimators. The record omits the total n for this experiment; the threshold M = n/d = 15 implies n = 1350.

rows.subject: distributed ridgeless regression estimator β̄M
rows.operation_detail: Reported the test-risk curve with peaks as the split count changes the local sample-size-to-dimension ratio.
rows.note: The caption describes peaks whenever d = n/M; numerical curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Same experiment family as r1. The caption states peaks wherever d = n/M, but gives no values. It may partly duplicate r1 (Fig. 2 right).

rows.subject: distributed ridgeless regression estimator β̄M
rows.operation_detail: Derived a lower bound for excess risk as a function of d and the local sample count n/M.
rows.measure: lower bound on excess risk: τ̃² min{d,n/M} / [(n/M) max{d,n/M} + 1 − min{d,n/M}]
rows.value: The text states that the bound has peaks at d = n/M, with height at least τ̃² M/d.
rows.locator: Appendix B.2, Theorem B.6 and accompanying text
rows.note: This is a lower bound, not a report that the actual test risk equals the bound or has the same curve.
rows.check: This is a theoretical lower bound (Theorem B.6), not a measured risk. It shows a peak in the bound at d = n/M but cannot show the second descent of the actual risk.

relationships.condition: MSDYear (d = 90) distributed ridgeless linear regression, sweeping the number of splits M through the local interpolation threshold n/M = d
relationships.reason: r1 and r2 report test error rising up to M = n/d and falling as local overparameterization increases. Figure-only, no numbers; the decline is confounded with averaging over M.
relationships.display_finding: Test error rose up to M=n/d and fell with increasing local overparameterization, although averaging over more splits also increased.
